memory_candidates: In CS5ModalAxiom (Constructive/CS5.lean), there is no dual of tBox (box-X imp X) for the diamond -- dia-X imp X is not a theorem and is false in general (would force every accessible world to agree with the root on every atom). Any soundness proof that needs to 'shed' an outer diamond wrapping an arbitrary formula (not just bot, which is absorbing under efq) is blocked in bare CS5; this affects any nested-sequent rule whose InputCtx.fillLhs recursion inserts unbounded dia layers, e.g. the id and orL constructors in Cslib/Logics/Modal/Metalogic/Constructive/Nested/Rules.lean when their surrounding OutputCtx (Lambda) has length >= 2.

dia(X or Y) imp (dia X or dia Y) (disjunction distributing over diamond) is exactly IS5ModalAxiom's kdisj (Intuitionistic/IS5.lean:121), deliberately absent from CS5ModalAxiom -- this is not an oversight but a genuine strength difference between IS5 and CS5, confirmed by failed derivation attempts using k/kdia/tBox/tDia/fourBox/fourDia/bBox/bDia.

When bridging two different OutputCtx filling operations (fillFull vs fillRhs) whose recursions BOTH bottom out through .box (not .dia), the bridge is generally resolvable via tBox (for the base-case box-vs-no-box mismatch) plus curry/uncurry combinators (for the singleton-case comma-order mismatch) -- this resolved Nested/Soundness.lean's impR case (Phase 12), which Phase 11 had flagged as needing 'a genuinely separate bridging induction' but which turned out to need no new axiom at all. This is a materially easier class of bridge than one involving InputCtx.fillLhs's .dia-based recursion (id/orL's blocked cases), where no such box-collapsing trick (tBox) has a diamond-side dual.

A useful diagnostic for whether a nested-sequent soundness case is tractable in CS5: does its Lean encoding route the unbounded ambient context through OutputCtx.fillFull/fillRhs (both .box-based recursion, tBox-bridgeable) or through InputCtx.fillLhs (dia-based recursion past depth 1, generally NOT bridgeable for a non-absorbing target)? Zero-premise 'axiom' rules (like id) and branching rules (like orL) that route through the latter are structurally at risk of needing an axiom CS5 does not have.
